changelog: [When to Segment]: Added explicit permissive rules to fix under-segmentation: (1) 그런데/근데/그래서/그러니까 always mark a valid split the instant the prior clause has a complete predicate, even if what follows is itself another connective-headed clause — segment at the FIRST such boundary, don't wait for a later one; (2) any -고/-며 coordination between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb (subject may be pro-dropped but recoverable from the immediately preceding NP) is always a valid split point, without waiting for confirmation from later material; (3) clarified that '?' or '.' occurring on a bare word/short phrase mid-utterance (not just after a full sentence) is still a mandatory split candidate.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed two over-broad prohibitions that were causing missed splits: the 'duplicated discourse marker' rule now only blocks a boundary when the identical marker token repeats with NO intervening complete clause between the two occurrences (not just general co-occurrence); the 'dependent NP list' rule now only blocks bare noun-phrase lists with no verb at all, and explicitly no longer applies once the following material contains its own complete predicate — such cases must be split per the new coordinate-clause rule in [When to Segment].
